chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Muhammad, who said:
I asked him about lodging with the people of the kharaj (land tax), so he said: 'They are lodged with them for three days.'
ai.seo_question: How long should tax collectors stay with the taxpayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the customary practice (urf) for tax collectors, limiting their stay with landowners to three days to prevent financial burden and harassment. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in public administration, ensuring that state officials do not overstay their welcome or impose undue hardship on the taxpayers.
